enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
525 AM MDT Fri Oct 23 2026

...New AVIATION, FIRE WEATHER...

.KEY MESSAGES...
Updated at 530 AM MDT Fri Oct 23 2026

 - A rare late-season risk of strong to severe thunderstorms will
   occur this evening. Widespread showers and thunderstorms
   developing across the South-Central New Mexico and Far West 
   Texas between 2 and 10 PM. Storms will be capable of large 
   hail, damaging winds, and localized flash flooding. 

 - More storm chances over the weekend, mostly east of the Rio 
   Grande. Highest local risks across Otero and Hudspeth Counties.

 - Drier weather expected early next week, but another round of
   rain chances looks likely after next Wednesday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1100 PM MDT Thu Oct 22 2026

WV imagery showing main upper low now over western Nevada. Low 
will continue lifting out northward as a secondary low eventually 
closes off over SoCal and Arizona. Leading trough from the low 
extends N-S along the AZ/NM state line with good drying behind it.
This trough delineates the western edge of this evening's 
convection. A weakening surface front from western Arizona down 
across the Baja will continue east possibly near the AZ/NM before 
washing out. The upper trough will continue to slowly drifting 
east over central New Mexico Friday afternoon before washing out. 
This will usher drier air into the western CWA (PWs of around .6 
inches compared to 1.0 inch in the east). Decent CAPE values will 
continue Friday, along with some speed shear. Thus expect 
scattered convection again from about Deming east, with more 
isolated storms to the west, though some severe storms still 
possible either side of this line. 

Saturday and Sunday...upper low continues to slowly lift 
northward from Arizona up to southern Utah. This will push deeper 
layered moisture east of the RG Valley, where decent chances of 
storms will continue. Expect best storm coverage from the RG 
Valley, with just isolated showers/storms to the west. Lowering 
PWs all areas suggest less chance of heavy rain/flooding. Some 
severe storm potential will continue but should be limited mostly 
to the RG Valley east. 

Monday and Tuesday...main upper low exits into the central Plains
with drier air aloft (at least at upper levels). GFS shows mid-
level winds (700mb) remaining southerly and keeping some shallower
moisture in the eastern CWA, with a slight chance of showers 
Monday from El Paso east. Moisture clears out Tuesday as mid level
winds briefly turn more southwest. 

Wednesday and Thursday...GFS remains bullish in bringing up more 
moisture with the help of a Pacific short wave approaching the 
area. Thus GFS has west two days here while the ECMWF remains 
mostly dry.

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 530 AM MDT Fri Oct 23 2026

High risk of direct TS impacts at KELP and S NM sites this 
evening. Forecast beginning with FEW060, FEW-SCT250 this morning. 
Surface winds 140-180 at 5 to 10 knots. CB developing over 
northern Chihuahua and S NM after 20Z this afternoon, likely 
reaching KELP/KLRU 22-02Z. TS moving to the NE at 40 mph. 
Temporary IFR VIS due to +TSRA and gusts up to 40 knots possible. 
TAF amendments are likely this timeframe. Conditions expected to 
improve after 04Z tonight, with lingering SHRA through midnight, 
then clear early Saturday morning.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 530 AM MDT Fri Oct 23 2026

Low fire danger due to recent rains. Prevailing wind out of the
SSE at 5 to 10 mph, with Good vent rates today. Scattered showers
and thunderstorms again this afternoon, mostly affecting south- 
central New Mexico and Lincoln NF. Some storms will be severe 
between 2-8PM, with large hail and damaging wind gusts.

Rain chances shift east over the weekend, leading to a mostly dry
Gila NF and Western NM, but widespread storms continuing for 
Southeast NM and Lincoln NF. Storm motions to the NE at 30-40 mph
will reduce flood risk somewhat, though localized flooding 
remains possible. Monday-Wednesday look drier, but rain chances
return quickly by the end of next week.

&&
